domain_restrictions: a, b, r are integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0.
The family e_i is only defined for indices i from 1 through b.
For i from 1 through b, e_i equals i when i <= a and equals r + i when a < i <= b.
d must be a positive integer whenever M_d is used or divisibility by d is discussed.
M_d(u, v) counts integers m with u < m <= v and d dividing m, where u and v are integers.
The counts in the conclusion are taken over the finite index set from 1 through b.
If b = 0, the index set from 1 through b is empty, so the counted sets are empty.
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every choice of integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, if every positive integer d has at least as many multiples in the interval from r + a to r + b as in the interval from a to b, then for every positive integer d the number of indices i from 1 through b for which d divides e_i is at least the number of indices i from 1 through b for which d divides i.
quantifier_order: Fix integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0.
For each integer i with 1 <= i <= b, define e_i by a piecewise rule: e_i = i if i <= a, and e_i = r + i if a < i <= b.
For each positive integer d and integers u, v, define M_d(u, v) as the number of integers m satisfying u < m <= v and d divides m.
Assume that for every positive integer d, M_d(r + a, r + b) is at least M_d(a, b).
Conclude that for every positive integer d, the number of indices i from 1 through b with d dividing e_i is at least the number of indices i from 1 through b with d dividing i.

statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. For 1 <= i <= b define an integer e_i by e_i = i when i <= a, and e_i = r+i when a < i <= b. For each positive integer d define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|. If M_d(r+a, r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d, then for every positive integer d one has |{i in {1,...,b} : d divides e_i}| >= |{i in {1,...,b} : d divides i}|.
